# @kodel-ai/opencode-plugin

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin for [Kodel AI](https://kodel.ai). It registers Kodel's chat and Codex model providers (served by the Kodel server's `ai-proxy`) and adds the `kodel` MCP server, so the agent can use Kodel tools.

## What it does

- **Authentication** — stores a Kodel Personal Access Token (PAT) and your Kodel server URL.
- **Provider `kodel`** — all chat models through `{host}/ai-proxy/v1` (Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible models via `/messages`).
- **Provider `kodel-responses`** — Codex models through `/responses`. Registered only when the catalog contains such models.
- **MCP server `kodel`** — connects to `{host}/api/mcp` and exposes Kodel tools (tasks, pipelines, repositories, knowledge base, …). If a `.kodel.json` is found in the repository, requests carry an `X-Project-Id` header.
- **Model capabilities** — the model catalog (`/ai-proxy/v1/models`) reports per-model capabilities (image/PDF input, tool calling, token limits), and the plugin passes them to OpenCode, so vision models accept images and PDFs.
- **Resilient startup** — if the server answers `401` while an instance is still starting, the model catalog is retried for about 15 seconds instead of leaving the provider empty.
- **Agent status reporting** — inside a Kodel-managed environment (when `KODEL_SESSION_ID` is set) the plugin reports whether the agent is working, idle or waiting for input. It does nothing otherwise.

## Compatibility

One package works with both OpenCode generations:

| OpenCode                                       | Entry point                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| v1 (1.18.29 and newer; older v1 also loads it) | `server(input)` — `config`, `auth`, `event` and `tool.execute.before` hooks             |
| v2 (beta, `2.0.x`)                             | `setup(ctx)` — `ctx.integration`, `ctx.provider`, `ctx.mcp`, `ctx.event` and `ctx.tool` |

OpenCode v1 plugins do not run on v2, so the plugin ships both implementations in a single default export `{ id, server, setup }`. See the [v1 → v2 plugin migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/migrate-v1).

## Requirements

- OpenCode v1 (1.18.29 or newer) or v2.
- A reachable Kodel server exposing `/ai-proxy/v1/models`, `/ai-proxy/v1/messages` (Anthropic API), `/ai-proxy/v1/responses` (Codex) and `/api/mcp`.
- A Kodel Personal Access Token with access to the project you work on (create one in the web UI: profile → Personal Access Tokens).

## Installation

Add the plugin to `opencode.json` (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or the project root). OpenCode installs the package on the next start.

OpenCode v1:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@kodel-ai/opencode-plugin"]
}
```

OpenCode v2:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["@kodel-ai/opencode-plugin"]
}
```

## Login

OpenCode v1:

```bash
opencode auth login
# provider: kodel
# Kodel server URL → e.g. http://localhost:3000 or https://kodel.company.com
# Enter your API key → your Kodel PAT
```

The credentials are stored in OpenCode's `auth.json`:

- Linux: `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json`)
- macOS: `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` (OpenCode uses `xdg-basedir` on every platform)

OpenCode v2:

```bash
opencode auth
# integration: Kodel
# Kodel server URL → the "host" form field
# key → your Kodel PAT
```

On v2 the credentials are kept by OpenCode itself. If no Kodel connection exists, the plugin falls back to a v1-style `auth.json`.

On v2 the plugin refreshes the providers when the credentials change; if the models do not show up after logging in, restart OpenCode. On v1 restart OpenCode after logging in.

## Link a repository to a Kodel project (optional)

Put a `.kodel.json` in the repository root. The plugin looks for it upward from the working directory (up to 20 levels):

```json
{
  "projectId": "PLT",
  "apiUrl": "http://localhost:3000"
}
```

MCP calls then carry `X-Project-Id: PLT`, so the `kodel` MCP tools work in the context of that project without naming it explicitly.

## Disabling the MCP server

The `kodel` MCP server gives the model Kodel tools (tasks, instances, …). If you do not need them, turn them off with OpenCode's own settings; the model providers keep working.

### Turn the server off completely

The plugin honors OpenCode's standard flag. Put it in the global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (all projects) or in a project `opencode.json`.

OpenCode v1:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@kodel-ai/opencode-plugin"],
  "mcp": {
    "kodel": { "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

OpenCode v2 reads `disabled: true` (the plugin also understands the v1 spelling `enabled: false`):

```json
{
  "plugins": ["@kodel-ai/opencode-plugin"],
  "mcp": {
    "kodel": { "disabled": true }
  }
}
```

The plugin then does not register the server at all, and no connection to `{host}/api/mcp` is made.

### Only hide the tools from the model

If the connection should stay but the tools must not reach the model's context (a common cause of hallucinations around unneeded tools), use OpenCode's glob filter. It applies at runtime on top of the plugin:

```json
{
  "tools": { "kodel_*": false }
}
```

You can disable tools globally and enable them for a specific agent — see [OpenCode: MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/).

## Verifying the setup

```bash
opencode
# /models — kodel/<model> (and kodel-responses/<model> if Codex models exist) should be listed
# /mcp    — the kodel server shows as connected (absent if it is disabled)
```

## Plugin logs

On v1 the plugin logs through OpenCode's native logger (`client.app.log`). Traces (chosen host, the `/models` request, provider registration, skipped MCP) are written at `debug` level, so they stay out of the normal output; they go to OpenCode's log files (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/`) and show with `--log-level DEBUG`:

```bash
opencode --log-level DEBUG
```

At `warn` only real problems remain: a missing or invalid credential entry and a model-catalog request that still fails after the retries.

The v2 entry has no `client.app.log`: warnings go to stderr, and traces are printed when `KODEL_OC_DEBUG=1`.
